newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity settles mixed after rise fizzles.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity settles mixed after rise fizzles.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures settled mixed Thursday after an early rise fizzled when buying interest dried up by late morning.

"There were rumors of one or two players buying blocks of power. People panicked to cover their short positions. Then, there was no one left buying after the short covering was over," a Houston trader explained.
August Palo Verde (PV) closed down 20 cents at $35.86, but did hit a new contract high of $37.30 in early trade.
September PV fell 30 cents to close at $29.85, while October lost 15 cents to settle at $23.75.
August California Oregon Border (COB) fell 42 cents to close at $22.91, after hitting a high of $23.50.
September COB lost 26 cents to close at $22.83, while October fell 5 cents to close at $21.85.
NYMEX estimated 750 PV and 366 COB contracts had traded.
Sources said the upcoming restart of several power generating units was leading to caution in the futures market.
In generation news, the 750 megawatt (MW) unit 2 at the Mohave coal-fired power plant in Nevada remained off line with no estimate as to how long it would be shut.
The unit, which tripped off Monday due to a boiler tube leak, had been expected to restart late Wednesday night, but the discovery of additional tube leaks led to the delay.
Also, the 1,158 MW WNP-2 nuclear power plant in Washington state was taken off-line early Wednesday for generator repairs.
The unit is in the process of restarting from an extended refueling outage that began in late March. Due to extensive testing requirements, WNP-2 is not expected to be fully on-line before next week.
The 1,073 MW unit 2 at the Diablo Canyon nuclear power plant in California reached 90 percent power as of early Thursday and was expected to reach full power by mid-day.
A 750 MW unit at the Four Corners coal-fired power plant in New Mexico will be shut Friday for three weeks for repairs.
The 1,070 MW unit 2 and 1,080 MW unit 3 at the San Onofre nuclear plant in Southern California were scheduled to restart July 15 and 17, respectively.
Weather in the Southwest was forecast to remain dry and sunny through early next week, with temperatures averaging near normal to five degrees F above normal.
The six to 10-day outlook for the Southwest called for above normal temperatures in western sections and near normal for eastern areas.

Coastal sections of the Pacific Northwest were expected to see near normal temperatures through early next week, while areas east of the Continental Divide were expected to experience temperatures eight to 16 degrees below normal.
In the six to 10-day forecast, temperatures in the Northwest were expected to average above normal.
